plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Self-serve pay-as-you-go account, no platform fee; GPU quota may need a request.

caveats: Azure Retail Prices API eastus Linux list. Windows excluded. Spot snapshot not guaranteed. Reservations API retailPrice is TOTAL commitment despite 1 Hour unit label, not hourly! VM CPU/RAM bundled; managed disks/network/IP extra.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit): single-GPU H100 via Standard_NC40ads_H100_v5 (H100 NVL 94 GB): on-demand eastus $6.98/h, northeurope $8.376/h (cheapest EU checked), Spot eastus $1.289904/h (snapshot), reserved 1y $5.23505/h, 3y $3.839/h. Before this only 8-GPU ND H100 v5 nodes were carded.

2026-09-28 (fix batch): 8-GPU ND96 nodes now priced per GPU (node price / 8, Azure Retail Prices API eastus) with gpu_min_count 8; reserved regimes flagged commit (self-serve reservations, not sales) with hourly = term total / term hours. alt removed from all GPU instances.

Azure free account gives $200 credit for 30 days, but Free Trial subscriptions cannot raise quota or use Spot, so it does not realistically cover A100/H100/ND nodes; deliberately not modelled as one_time_credit on this GPU card.

fleet.verification: Azure signup uses phone and non-prepaid card for identity verification.
fleet.tiers: Free Trial: no quota increases, no Spot. Pay-as-you-go: default ~20 vCPU/region total + per-family + separate 20-core Spot quota; raise via My quotas (auto-review) or support ticket. EA defaults 350.
fleet.notes: Regional total vCPU and VM-family vCPU quotas both apply, plus VM-count quotas. Applied values depend on subscription/region; no universal fresh-account numeric quota verified. Portal quota request may require review. GPU capacity is not guaranteed by approval.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Hibernation is triggered on a VM using the Azure portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs, or APIs.
snapshot_auto.note: Stop/deallocate keeps managed disks (persistent_disk) but takes no snapshot; the memory-preserving mode (hibernation) is user-triggered. Scheduled Azure Backup / snapshot policies exist but are backups, not state-on-stop.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: An Azure managed disk snapshot is a full, read-only copy of a managed disk. Use a snapshot as a point-in-time backup or to help troubleshoot virtual machine (VM) issues. You can take a snapshot of either an operating system (OS) disk or a data disk. These snapshots exist independently of the source disk, and you can use them to create new managed disks.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk only, no memory; new VMs can boot from a disk created from the snapshot ('use the managed disk as the OS disk for a new VM'). Also VM restore points (multi-disk, crash- or application-consistent, via REST API). Hibernation (memory saved to OS disk, resume later) is a separate on-demand stop, only on NVv4 and NVadsA10v5 GPU series with up to 112 GB RAM, and is not a forkable snapshot.

harness_api.quote: Run Command can run scripts on your virtual machines remotely by using the VM agent.
harness_api.note: Only generic script execution (Run Command, extensions); no first-party agent-harness API for VMs.

egress_allowlist.quote: A network security group contains security rules that allow or deny inbound network traffic to, or outbound network traffic from, several types of Azure resources.
egress_allowlist.note: NSG outbound rules: IP/CIDR/service tag/port (5-tuple). Domain level via Azure Firewall (separately billed): 'Application FQDN filtering rules : You can limit outbound HTTP/S traffic or Azure SQL traffic to a specified list of fully qualified domain names (FQDN) including wild cards.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/features). Both enforced outside the VM.

egress_http_rules.quote: URL filtering : Extends FQDN filtering to consider the entire URL, including any additional path.
egress_http_rules.note: Azure Firewall Premium only, needs TLS inspection with a customer CA for HTTPS paths; path/URL and web-category rules. No method/header rules documented.

ingress_rules.quote: You can specify Any, an individual IP address, a CIDR block (for example, 10.0.0.0/24), a service tag , or an application security group .
ingress_rules.note: NSG inbound rules on NIC/subnet; public IP optional (private-only VMs possible).

guest_firewall.note: Full Hyper-V VM with root; iptables/nftables work inside the guest.

secret_proxy.quote: The Azure Key Vault virtual machine (VM) extension automatically refreshes certificates stored in an Azure key vault. The extension monitors a list of observed certificates stored in key vaults. When the extension detects a change, it retrieves and installs the corresponding certificates.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets reach the VM via Key Vault + managed identity or the Key Vault extension, i.e. they enter the machine. No credential-injecting egress proxy (Azure Firewall TLS inspection does not inject credentials).

volume_attach.quote: This article shows you how to attach both new and existing disks to a Linux virtual machine through the Azure portal.
volume_attach.note: Managed data disks (Standard HDD/SSD, Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2, Ultra), count limited per VM size; billed separately.

volume_shared.quote: Azure shared disks is a feature for Azure managed disks that allows you to attach a managed disk to multiple virtual machines (VMs) simultaneously.
volume_shared.note: Shared disks: block-level read-write on several VMs (needs a cluster-aware FS/SCSI PR; Ultra, Premium SSD v2, Premium SSD, Standard SSD only). Azure Files: 'You can mount Azure file shares concurrently from cloud and on-premises clients' via SMB/NFS, read-write (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-introduction). Blob NFS/BlobFuse also available.

isolation.quote: Azure virtual machines run on the Hyper-V hypervisor, giving each customer VM a dedicated, isolated virtual machine.
isolation.note: Full VM isolation via Microsoft's Hyper-V hypervisor (root/host partition model), not container/gVisor/microVM.

image_oci.quote: Azure enables you to bring a VHD to the platform to use as a managed disk by using the Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell module.
image_oci.note: Custom VM images use the VHD/managed-disk format, not OCI/Docker images. Containers can be built and run inside the VM (see docker_inside), but the VM itself does not boot from an OCI image.

docker_inside.quote: Standard_NC-series and other GPU VMs support NVIDIA Container Toolkit / Docker with GPU passthrough for containerized workloads.
docker_inside.note: Full Linux VM with root; Docker/containerd installs and runs normally, including NVIDIA Docker for GPU containers.

desktop.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
desktop.note: not offered: the GPU VM product is bare IaaS compute; there is no managed desktop/VNC/RDP streaming service bundled (users may self-install RDP/X11 inside the VM, but that is not a provided feature).

browser.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (raw GPU/CPU VM compute, no managed browser).

computer_use.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (IaaS VM, no screenshot/click driving API).

anti_bot.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (GPU/VM compute, not a browsing/scraping product).

captcha_solving.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (GPU/VM compute, not a browsing/scraping product).

egress_ip_type.quote: Public IP addresses allow Internet resources to communicate inbound to Azure resources and allow Azure resources to communicate outbound to Internet and public-facing Azure services.
egress_ip_type.note: Standard datacenter-range public IPs assigned from Azure's own address space.

fork.quote: An Azure managed disk snapshot is a full, read-only copy of a managed disk. ... These snapshots exist independently of the source disk, and you can use them to create new managed disks.
fork.note: No one-call 'fork this machine' API; cloning requires generalizing/capturing an image or snapshotting a disk and deploying a new VM from it, a multi-step manual process, not a native fork primitive.

fork_running.quote: It's recommended that the VM be stopped/deallocated prior to taking a snapshot to ensure the disk is in a consistent state.
fork_running.note: Capturing a generalized image for reuse requires the source VM to be stopped/deallocated; no supported clone-while-running-with-processes-intact feature.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Hibernation is triggered on a VM using the Azure portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs, or APIs.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Hibernation preserves memory to disk for resume on the SAME VM (and only on select NV/NVads-A10 series); it is not a mechanism to clone a machine's live memory state into new running instances.

wake_on_request.quote: A VM that's in the Stopped or Stopped (deallocated) state must be explicitly started to run workloads again.
wake_on_request.note: Stopped/deallocated VMs require an explicit start action; there is no automatic wake triggered by an inbound network request.

auto_stop_idle.quote: You aren't billed for a VM while it's in the Stopped (deallocated) state, but you're billed while it's in the Stopped state.
auto_stop_idle.note: Azure VMs have no built-in idle-detection auto-stop; users can configure 'Auto-shutdown' on a fixed daily schedule (portal feature) but that is a scheduled shutdown, not idle-triggered.

live_resize.quote: Even when deallocation isn't required, changing the size of a running VM will cause it to restart.
live_resize.note: Resizing a running VM (changing CPU/RAM/GPU count via SKU change) always causes a restart; not a live/no-downtime resize.

agent_harnesses.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the GPU VM marketplace does not ship preinstalled coding-agent harness templates (Claude Code, Codex, etc.).

own_agent_api.quote: Run Command can run scripts on your virtual machines remotely by using the VM agent.
own_agent_api.note: Only generic remote script execution via the VM agent; no first-party browser/computer-use/research task-agent API for this product.

mcp_server.quote: Azure Virtual Machines is one of several types of on-demand, scalable computing resources that Azure offers.
mcp_server.note: No first-party MCP server ships specifically to control Azure GPU VMs; management is via ARM/CLI/SDK/portal.

lang_python.quote: The Data Science Virtual Machine (DSVM) is a customized VM image ... pre-installed and configured with several popular tools ... Python.
lang_python.note: Base Ubuntu marketplace images ship python3 by default, and Microsoft also offers pre-built Data Science VM images with Python/CUDA preinstalled for GPU workloads.

lang_node.quote: All VMs are identical — same size, image, and configuration.
lang_node.note: Standard Ubuntu/GPU marketplace base images do not ship Node.js by default; it must be installed by the user (unlike Python which ships on Ubuntu).

inbound_https.quote: Public IP addresses allow Internet resources to communicate inbound to Azure resources.
inbound_https.note: A public IPv4 plus an NSG rule opening port 443 lets any HTTPS server you run on the VM be reached; there is no managed HTTPS-URL-per-app layer, but inbound HTTPS to the machine is achievable and standard practice.

static_egress_ip.quote: A Standard SKU public IP address ... is static and won't change over the lifecycle of the resource.
static_egress_ip.note: A Standard SKU public IP (or NAT Gateway public IP) assigned to the VM/subnet is static and used for both inbound and outbound traffic.

macos.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Azure GPU VMs (NC/ND/NV series) run Linux or Windows guest OS only, no macOS VM offering.

arm64.note: All Azure GPU VM families (NC/ND/NV) use x86-64 (Intel/AMD) hosts; Azure's ARM64 VMs (Dpsv5/Epsv5, Cobalt) are a separate, non-GPU CPU line.

self_host.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Azure VMs run only in Microsoft-operated Azure datacenters (Azure Stack is a distinct hybrid product, not this GPU VM SKU line).

byoc.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; this is Microsoft's own hyperscaler cloud, not a managed service deployed into a customer's separate cloud account.

open_source.quote: Get the flexibility of virtualisation for a wide range of computing solutions with on-demand, scalable computing resources.
open_source.note: Azure Virtual Machines is a proprietary managed cloud service, not an open-source project.

soc2.quote: Microsoft Azure, Dynamics 365, Microsoft Power Platform, Microsoft 365, and other Microsoft online services undergo regular SOC 1, SOC 2, and SOC 3 audits.
soc2.note: Azure has SOC 2 Type II attestation covering Azure services including Virtual Machines.

hipaa.quote: Microsoft offers a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) as part of its online services terms to all customers who are subject to HIPAA/HITECH.
hipaa.note: Azure (including Virtual Machines) is covered under Microsoft's HIPAA BAA.

sso.quote: Microsoft Entra ID supports establishing single sign-on to applications ... using protocols such as SAML, WS-Federation, or OpenID Connect.
sso.note: Azure account/subscription access (portal, CLI, ARM) is via Microsoft Entra ID which supports SAML/OIDC SSO.

max_session_h.quote: A VM that's in the Running state ... continues to run until it's explicitly stopped, restarted, or deleted.
max_session_h.note: On-demand/reserved VMs run indefinitely until the customer stops them; Spot VMs can be evicted at any time (30s notice) but that is capacity-based eviction, not a fixed session-length limit.

nested_virt.note: Confirmed on the official VM-size feature tables for the GPU series this card covers: Standard_NCadsH100v5, Standard_NDH100v5, and Standard_NCA100v4 series pages all list 'Nested Virtualization: Not Supported' (Azure Hyper-V nested virtualization requires specific host generations/sizes not exposed on these GPU SKUs). false is correct.

eu_data_residency.quote: if a customer provisions its tenant in the European Union or the United States, Microsoft will store Customer Data at rest only within that Geo.
eu_data_residency.note: Azure's official data-residency page states Microsoft commits to storing Customer Data at rest only within the EU Geo when a customer provisions there (e.g. northeurope/westeurope/swedencentral regions used elsewhere on this card for EU GPU pricing). This is a first-party, documented EU data-residency guarantee, so false is incorrect; should be true.
